title: 1.1.3 Your First Statement
description: Open the browser console, run five ready-made statements, then change two of them to print your own text. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Run the five statements
steps.instructions: Run the code below. Five messages appear in the console panel. This is your first time seeing a browser console print output.

steps.title: Change the fourth statement
steps.instructions: Change the text inside the FOURTH console.log statement to say something about yourself. Keep the statement as a console.log call.

steps.title: Change the fifth statement
steps.instructions: Change the text inside the FIFTH console.log statement to say something else about yourself. Keep it as a console.log call.

steps.title: Run again and check
steps.instructions: Run again and watch the console show your two new messages. Leave the first three statements exactly as they are.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "1.1.3 Your First Statement". The task they were given: Run the code below. Five messages appear in the console panel. This is your first time seeing a browser console print output. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
